findings.title: The frozen React adapter refuses an ejected create-react-app tree, and ejected CRA is a mainstream webpack-era React shape
findings.evidence: analyze reads builder "unknown"; plan and migrate both refuse with: React plan: this tree declares neither react-scripts nor a Vite configuration, so no frozen React adapter claims it. This flow refuses rather than guessing an origin toolchain.
findings.why: shlink-web-client v2.3.0 ejected: it carries config/ and scripts/ with its own webpack 4 configuration and does not declare react-scripts. The adapter keys admission on the react-scripts declaration or a Vite configuration.
findings.status: named gap — not fixed, no frozen-subtree edit was made
findings.costImpact: An application in this shape costs zero migration units because it never enters the pipeline. It also cannot be counted toward any per-application average until admission widens.

findings.title: The era cell, not the migration, is what stopped the baseline
findings.evidence: webpack 4 md4 hashing fails on Node 24 (ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED, remedied by NODE_OPTIONS=--openssl-legacy-provider), then node-sass 4.12.0 refuses the host outright: OS X Unsupported architecture (arm64) with Unsupported runtime (137).
findings.why: This host has exactly one Node era cell installed (v24.15.0). node-sass 4.x publishes no arm64 binding for a modern Node ABI, and the source tree is immutable corpus, so swapping it for dart-sass is not available.
findings.costImpact: Era-cell provisioning is a per-application, network-bearing, sometimes-impossible act on a single-architecture host. It is the first cost of a new application and it is not bounded by anything measured so far.

findings.title: Modern npm adds two per-application refusals a fleet runner must answer
findings.evidence: EALLOWREMOTE on a 2020 lockfile carrying an https tarball dependency (xdg-basedir from registry.yarnpkg.com), remedied by --allow-remote all; and install scripts skipped by default, which silently produced a tree whose native dependency was never built.
findings.costImpact: Two operator decisions per application before the first build. Both are mechanisable as policy, and both are today unwritten judgment.

findings.title: migrate materialises an entry document, not an installable migrated tree
findings.evidence: On the admitted comparator (sqlpad client) the materialised lane records 1 file written (index.html), 167 copied, 0 removed, and the lane's package.json still declares react-scripts ^3.4.1 with no Vite configuration.
findings.why: The Vite-era configuration and package rewrite for previously completed applications lives in per-application fixture code (react-linkfree-v0-72-0-vite8.ts 318 lines, react-hospitalrun-vite8.ts 272, react-memos-v0-1-3-vite8-run.ts 255, react-avataaars-vite8.config.ts 18), not in the operator flow.
findings.costImpact: The owner's ruling that install+build of the migrated tree cannot be manual lands here: the CLI does not yet emit a tree that can be installed and built, so this stage is per-application authoring by construction, not by habit.

verdict.outcome: bounded — no application reached a migrated build or a witness pass inside this spike, so the post-industrialization per-application cost is still unmeasured; what was measured is that two of the three stages before it stopped on a never-completed application, one at the frozen adapter's admission gate and one at the era-cell wall
verdict.statement: ~3 units per application is not established. It is not refuted either: the claim was never reached, because the application chosen at random from the never-completed set never got as far as the stage the ~3u estimate describes. On this attempt the cost of the pre-migration stages alone was 37 seconds of machine time against about 22 minutes of operator time across four refusals, and the run ended with zero builds, zero witness passes and zero new TypeScript lines.
whatRemainsManual: Era-cell provisioning — choosing and obtaining a Node/toolchain era that the application's own native dependencies support. Cost here: two failed builds, about 4 minutes of operator time, and no remedy available on this host.
Install policy decisions — the remote-tarball allowance and the install-script allowance. Cost here: one failed install, about 3 minutes of operator time.

Adapter admission judgment for trees outside the react-scripts/Vite declaration — today a refusal an operator must read and route. Cost here: about 2 minutes of operator time, and the application leaves the pipeline.
The Vite-era configuration and package rewrite for an admitted tree — still per-application fixture authoring (18 to 318 lines on the applications already done).
Witness journey authoring and calibration — untouched by this spike and therefore still carrying T002's reading, in which it is the dominant per-application authorship.
verdict.budgetNote: The unit's wall-clock budget (60 minutes) bound this run; the 3-round calibration budget was never reached because no witness pass started.

notEstablished: No build ran to completion here, so nothing in this record establishes that either application builds on any era cell.
No witness pass ran, so nothing here establishes browser behaviour, parity, locality, or a bounded witness outcome for either application.
The thin-wrapper line counts are an inventory of files already on disk from previously completed applications; they are not a measurement of what a new application costs.
The operator timings are single-run wall clock on one host, not a distribution; the sibling spike's medians over 12 applications remain the better reading of operator machine time.
The refusals recorded here are readings of this host and this pin. A different architecture, a different Node era cell, or a later npm would produce different refusals, and none of them was tested.
Nothing here revises the frozen adapters, the supported matrix, or any capability's status; no coverage or matrix artifact was regenerated.
